title: Hosted API demo - chat/text generation basics (streaming, params, retries)

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Acme Head of Platforms), Sasha Li (Security Architect), Ravi Kumar (ML Engineer), Emily Park (Product)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted API walkthrough; demo of streaming chat; covered params and retry semantics; security/Qs; agreed to pilot + follow ups.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex, AE at Redwood. Priya and I will run through the hosted API demo - we'll show chat/text basics, streaming, parameters and retry behavior. 
[00:18] Jordan Miles: Hey thanks Alex, excited. We're evaluating latency/cost because this will be customer-facing in our risk dashboard. Sasha from security is here too.
[00:28] Sasha Li: Hi, yeah quick note: we need to understand KMS integration, retention, and SOC2 evidence.
[00:35] Alex Chen: Totally - we'll hit those. Priya, want to kick off with the quick architecture overview?
[00:40] Priya Patel: Sure. So Redwood Hosted API is a simple REST/SDK surface - you can call /v1/generate or chat endpoints. For streaming we open a chunked response, you get partial tokens as they're generated. Key knobs are temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and also stability params for chat-turn continuity.
[01:05] Ravi Kumar: When you say streaming is it server-sent events or websockets?
[01:10] Priya Patel: Primarily chunked HTTP streaming and SSE in some SDKs; websockets are supported in some private setups. For hosted it's chunked streaming over HTTPS.
[01:20] Emily Park: How do retries work if the stream drops mid-response?
[01:25] Priya Patel: Good question. We recommend idempotent request tokens. If a connection dies mid-stream you can re-issue with the same request_id and a resume token in some SDKs; otherwise we retry from start with deterministic seeds and we also support checkpointing the KV cache for longer sessions.
[01:45] Jordan Miles: Checkpointing the what?
[01:48] Priya Patel: The KV cache, like key-value cache for decoder context. Sorry sometimes we say KV cache but it can show up in docs as key value cache or key-V cache - transcription note, heh. It's used to avoid re-computing prefix when resuming.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Quick qual question - what's your expected QPS and latency SLO for the pilot?
[02:12] Jordan Miles: For the risk assistant we expect bursty QPS up to 50 req/s and 95th percentile latency under 400ms ideally. Cost target is on par with our current token-cost budget; so we need batching and caching to be effective.
[02:30] Priya Patel: We can tune batching and automatic prefix caching; Redwood Optimize suggests batch sizes and quantization profiles to balance cost. For hosted API you can choose model variants to trade cost/latency.
[02:48] Sasha Li: On encryption - do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[02:52] Alex Chen: Hosted supports envelope encryption and we integrate with cloud KMS for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted we offer managed keys but can discuss Private deployment for CMKs if required. We'll send the encryption matrix in the security pack.
[03:10] Ravi Kumar: Any hard limits on token length? We have some long prompts for multi-turn.
[03:15] Priya Patel: Hosted supports up to 16k context on selected models, and we help with rolling window strategies plus KV caching for longer histories. For very large contexts we suggest quantized Dedicated variants.
[03:30] Alex Chen: Ok demo time - Priya's going to share her screen, we'll do a live chat demo and show streaming and param changes.
[03:38] [03:38] Priya Patel: (screen) Alright, hitting the SDK example. Example code: client.chat.create({model: 'rwd-chat-medium', messages: [...], stream: true, temperature: 0.2, top_p: 0.9}) - we open a stream and print chunks.
[04:05] [04:05] Priya Patel: Here you see chunks coming in every ~50-150ms, each chunk has partial tokens, we can show how to handle backpressure.
[04:22] Jordan Miles: Seems smooth - are there client libraries for Node/Python?
[04:26] Priya Patel: Yes Node/Python/Java and a lightweight Go SDK. We also have curl examples for quick testing.
[04:35] Sasha Li: Does the SDK handle retries automatically or do we need to implement our own backoff?
[04:39] Priya Patel: SDKs implement configurable retry with exponential backoff and jitter; default is conservative. We also recommend idempotency keys for operations that must not double-run.
[04:52] Ravi Kumar: How about partial generation duplication on retry - will it hallucinate if we restart?
[04:57] Priya Patel: If you use the same request_id and model deterministic_seed, outcomes are reproducible; otherwise you'll get a fresh generation. For production we usually recommend deterministic seeds for critical flows.
[05:12] Alex Chen: Quick pause - any concerns so far on cost/latency tradeoffs?
[05:17] Jordan Miles: Mainly cost at scale. We need predictable per-token billing and transparency.
[05:22] Alex Chen: Redwood provides token-level cost breakdowns in Console and the Optimize suggestions to reduce units. We'll share sample dashboards.
[05:33] Priya Patel: Back to demo - altering temperature from 0.2 to 0.8 increases diversity. I'll show a short example: same prompt, temp 0.2 versus 0.8 - see more exploratory completions at higher temp.
[05:55] [06:00] Priya Patel: Also note top_p vs temperature: they interact; choose one primary knob to control randomness. Typical prod configs are low temp (0.0-0.3) + small top_p adjustments.
[06:18] Emily Park: For our product we want consistent tone - so low temp makes sense. Any automatic scoring for quality/regressions?
[06:24] Priya Patel: Yes Optimize includes eval hooks; you can connect prompt sets and get regression alerts when output quality drifts.
[06:32] Jordan Miles: Security follow-up - Sasha any red flags?
[06:35] Alex Chen: Not yet, just need the SOC2 / pen test and encryption docs. Also data residency - can we have EU-only processing for certain datasets?
[06:24] Alex Chen: Yes region routing can pin requests to EU regions; for strict residency Private deployment is recommended.
[06:32] Jordan Miles: For the pilot we'd like Hosted to start but maybe move to Dedicated if throughput grows.
[06:36] Priya Patel: That's a common path. We support seamless model pinning and rollout policies so you can start hosted and later migrate to Dedicated or Private with the same API surface.
[06:50] [07:00] Priya Patel: Now a short deep-dive on retries: typical pattern - client detects disconnected stream, re-issue with same request_id, use resume token if available. If that's not possible we fallback to start-over but we log a duplicate attempt and can apply idempotency checks server-side.
[07:25] Ravi Kumar: How do you recommend handling websocket disconnects from mobile clients?
[07:28] Priya Patel: Mobile best practice: use short-lived streaming, send checkpoints to server or use resumable HTTP streams. Also batch small requests when possible to reduce connection churn.
[07:42] Jordan Miles: On benchmarking - can Redwood run a sample against our data to measure latency?
[07:46] Alex Chen: Yes we can run a hosted benchmark with a small keys dataset or you can run the benchmark template we'll send. For Dedicated we can run on reserved GPUs for an apples-to-apples test.
[07:58] Emily Park: What about tokenization differences? We use subword tokens for embeddings.
[08:02] Priya Patel: We expose tokenizer utilities in SDK and Console so you can pre-calc token counts to estimate cost.
[08:10] [08:10] Alex Chen: Alright quick Q/A from security - Sasha any red flags?
[08:15] Sasha Li: Not yet, just need the SOC2 / pen test and encryption docs. Also data residency - can we have EU-only processing for certain datasets?
[08:24] Alex Chen: Yes region routing can pin requests to EU regions; for strict residency Private deployment is recommended.
[08:32] Jordan Miles: For the pilot we'd like Hosted to start but maybe move to Dedicated if throughput grows.
[08:36] Priya Patel: That's a common path. We support seamless model pinning and rollout policies so you can start hosted and later migrate to Dedicated or Private with the same API surface.
[08:50] [09:00] Priya Patel: Demo: showing retry in action - I'll intentionally drop the stream and re-issue with same id. You can see the resume token usage and consistent output.
[09:15] [09:15] (audio glitch) Speaker 1: uh sorry - can you repeat the resume token part?
[09:20] Priya Patel: Sure - resume token is returned periodically; client stores last token and provides it when reconnecting so server resumes from that token rather than starting over. Not all models support resume yet.
[09:36] Jordan Miles: If resume not supported, any recommended UX?
[09:39] Priya Patel: Show partial content and allow user to retry generation, or mark the turn incomplete and queue for re-generation. Depends on product needs.
[09:50] Ravi Kumar: Any limits on number of retries? To avoid runaway cost.
[09:53] Priya Patel: We recommend max 3 retries with exponential backoff by default. Console has policies to limit retries per-route.
[10:05] Alex Chen: Quick segue - error codes and observability?
[10:08] Priya Patel: We expose detailed error codes: rate_limit, transient_compute, model_incompatible, etc. Console traces each request and shows token counts and latency breakdown.
[10:20] Emily Park: Can we get per-route dashboards pushed to our Grafana?
[10:24] Alex Chen: We can export metrics to Prometheus/S3 and provide hooks for your monitoring stack.
[10:32] Jordan Miles: Pricing question - how granular is per-token billing and do you show cost per-route?
[10:36] Alex Chen: Token-level pricing and per-route cost breakdowns are in Console. For pilots we can provide sample cost projections.
[10:45] Sasha Li: Regarding compliance - do you do pen tests?
[10:48] Alex Chen: Yes, we run regular third-party pen tests; SOC2 Type II and ISO are in our security pack. We'll attach the latest reports.
[11:00] Priya Patel: Demo wrap-up - here's the sample code for streaming, and here's how to set temperature/top_p in the same request. Also showed deterministic_seed usage for reproducibility.
[11:15] [11:15] Jordan Miles: Good - this answered a lot. Two quick follow-ups: 1) We'll need the benchmark template; 2) Security docs + SOC2.
[11:24] Alex Chen: We'll send both. Also propose a 4-week pilot: ~50 req/s burst, 2 models (low-latency and cost-optimized), success metrics: 95th pctl < 400ms and cost <$X per 1k tokens (we'll estimate).
[11:40] Ravi Kumar: Sounds good. Who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[11:43] Alex Chen: Priya will be SE lead, Alex AE for logistics.
[11:48] Emily Park: Internal timeline - we can confirm sponsors by next week.
[11:52] Priya Patel: OK wrapping - I'll share the streaming snippet and a retry checklist.
[11:58] Alex Chen: Great thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps and action items, and we'll follow up by Friday with documents.
[12:10] Jordan Miles: Thanks all.
[12:12] Sasha Li: Thanks.

End of transcript.
